query: The Co-free FeNiCrMn system was selected to reduce cost while retaining the mechanical performance of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi; prior work reported comparable or better mechanical properties after excluding Co. Research on FeNiCrMn has mainly addressed corrosion, while studies of related high- and medium-entropy alloys examined dynamic responses under tension or compression, different temperatures and strain rates, compositional changes, and the presence of cracks or voids. Those studies established that dynamic properties are sensitive to loading regime and material condition, but their different chemistries and defect states do not identify what governs FeNiCrMn. Under the constraints of retaining the Co-free composition and its strength–ductility balance, what single testable mechanistic hypothesis explains the dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes? Define a controlled study capable of testing the hypothesis, its applicable boundaries, the prior findings that support it, and a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The dynamic behavior of solidified FeNiCrMn across temperature and strain-rate regimes is governed by a deformation mechanism involving dislocation nucleation and drag, which increases the strain rate sensitivity of the alloy at high strain rates.
generation.conditions: retaining Co-free composition and strength-ductility balance
generation.predicted_outcome: increased strain rate sensitivity at high strain rates
generation.boundary: temperature range: 300-1000 K, strain rate range: 10^-3 - 10^3 s^-1
generation.uncertainty: effect of grain size and precipitate distribution on deformation mechanism

falsification_experiment.design: uniaxial tensile testing at various temperatures and strain rates
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the strain rate sensitivity is not increased at high strain rates, the hypothesis is falsified, threshold: 10% increase in strain rate sensitivity

cited_evidence.text: Currently, several EHEA systems have been developed, including AlCoCrFeNi2.1 [], Al17Ni34Ti17V32 [], AlCr1.3TiNi2 [], and AlCrCuFeNi2 []. Owing to better practicality and low cost, the AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy, with similar microstructure and properties to the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy, was investigated. It is indicated that the AlCrFe2Ni2 alloy consists of the FCC and A2/B2 spinodal decomposition phase and presents better fracture strength and ductility []. In addition, the dynamic mechanical response of HEAs has also received a lot of attention. To use HEAs in extreme industrial environments, there is an urgent need for a comprehensive understanding of their performance and mechanisms during high-speed compression [,,,,]. According to the available literature, in addition to the dislocation-related mechanism, twinning mechanism, grain boundary-related mechanism, diffusion creep mechanism, and dynamic recrystallization mechanism, the shear bands are formed in HEAs at high strain rates or under large deformation conditions [,,,,]. High-entropy alloys (HEAs) are new alloys that contain five or more elements in roughly-equal proportion. We present new experiments and theory on the deformation behavior of HEAs under slow stretching (straining), and observe differences, compared to conventional alloys with fewer elements. For a specific range of temperatures and strain-rates, HEAs deform in a jerky way, with sudden slips that make it difficult to precisely control the deformation. An analytic model explains these slips as avalanches of slipping weak spots and predicts the observed slip statistics, stress-strain curves, and their dependence on temperature, strain-rate, and material composition. The ratio of the weak spots’ healing rate to the strain-rate is the main tuning parameter, reminiscent of the Portevin-LeChatellier effect and time-temperature superposition in polymers. Our model predictions agree with the experimental results. The proposed widely-applicable deformation mechanism is useful for deformation control and alloy design.
